key_lemmas.name: proposition_3_6
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Proposition 3.6. If }\widehat W\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\text{ is an }\epsilon\text{-nuclear norm stationary point of }f,\text{ then it is also an }\epsilon\text{-Frobenius norm stationary point of }f.\ \text{If }\widehat W\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\text{ is an }\epsilon\text{-Frobenius norm stationary point of }f,\text{ then it is also an }\sqrt r\epsilon\text{-nuclear norm stationary point of }f,\text{ where }r=\min\{m,n\}.
key_lemmas.role: Public endpoint and norm-stationarity bridge.

proof.description: Use the printed Frobenius/nuclear norm comparison for matrices of rank at most r.

For the nuclear-to-Frobenius direction, apply the printed norm comparison to A=\nabla f(\widehat W) and the Definition 3.5 hypothesis; the displayed substitution is derived, not printed in the proof window.

For the Frobenius-to-nuclear direction, apply the printed norm comparison to A=\nabla f(\widehat W) and the Definition 3.4 hypothesis; the displayed substitution is derived, not printed in the proof window.

proof.description: Record the two local conditions from the lemma statement as the branch hypotheses to be proved equivalent.

Bound the integral by the operator-norm bound and recover the M^{-1} to M smoothness inequality, completing (2) implies (1).

key_lemmas.name: lemma_4_12
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Lemma 4.12. If }f:\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is }1\text{-}\Lambda\text{-norm Lipschitz smooth with a positive definite matrix }\Lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},\text{ then }f\text{ is also }\|\Lambda\|_{op}\text{ Frobenius norm Lipschitz smooth and }\|\Lambda\|_*\text{ spectral norm Lipschitz smooth}.

key_lemmas.name: theorem_4_1
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Theorem 4.1. Under Assumptions 3.1 and 3.3, if we apply Algorithm 1 with }\eta_t=\eta,\text{ then }\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(W_t)\|_*]\le \frac{\mathbb{E}[f(W_0)-f(W_T)]}{T\eta}+\frac{Lr\eta}{2}+\frac{2\sigma\sqrt{r(1-\beta)}}{\sqrt{B(1+\beta)}}+\frac{2\sigma\sqrt r}{(1-\beta)T\sqrt B}+\frac{2r\eta\beta L}{1-\beta}.
key_lemmas.role: Public endpoint: stochastic Algorithm 1 under Frobenius smoothness.

proof.description: Apply Frobenius smoothness to one Algorithm 1 update with eta_t=eta.
Insert and subtract M_t inside the inner product and use the rank bound on the Frobenius norm square of U_tV_t^top.
Bound the inserted error inner product by Frobenius Cauchy-Schwarz.
Use the SVD identity for M_t to turn the search-direction inner product into ||M_t||_* and bound ||U_tV_t^top||_F by sqrt r.
Apply the nuclear-norm triangle inequality to replace ||M_t||_* by ||nabla f(W_t)||_* with one more tracking-error term.
Define C_t and invoke Lemma A.4 for the stochastic momentum tracking part.
Expand C_t in the deterministic lag term for t>0 using C_t=\beta C_{t-1}+(1-\beta)\nabla f(W_t).
Factor out beta from the preceding display.
Add and subtract the previous true gradient and apply the Frobenius triangle inequality.
Use Assumption 3.1 to bound the true-gradient difference by the Frobenius iterate difference.
Substitute the Algorithm 1 update and use the printed Frobenius bound \|U_{t-1}V_{t-1}^\top\|_F\le\sqrt r.
proof.ref: B.1 update and Frobenius norm substitution

proof.description: Unroll the recursion to the initial lag C_0=\nabla f(W_0) and the finite geometric sum.
Use C_0=\nabla f(W_0) and bound the finite geometric sum by \beta/(1-\beta).
Combine the stochastic tracking and deterministic lag bounds by the triangle inequality.
Substitute the combined tracking bound into the one-step descent inequality.
Sum over t=0,...,T-1 and bound the geometric beta sum.

key_lemmas.name: corollary_4_2
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Corollary 4.2. Under the same assumptions as Theorem 4.1, we have the following convergence guarantees for Algorithm 1: Stochastic setting: If }B=1,\eta=\sqrt{\frac{(1-\beta)\Delta}{rTL}},\text{ and }1-\beta=\min\left\{\frac{\sqrt{L\Delta}}{\sigma\sqrt T},1\right\},\text{ then }\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(W_t)\|_*]\le O\left(\sqrt[4]{\frac{r^2L\Delta\sigma^2}{T}}+\sqrt{\frac{rL\Delta}{T}}+\frac{\sqrt r\sigma^2}{\sqrt{L\Delta T}}\right).\ \text{Deterministic setting }(\sigma=0):\text{ If }\eta=\sqrt{\frac{\Delta}{rTL}},\beta=O(1),\text{ then }\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|\nabla f(W_t)\|_*\le O\left(\sqrt{\frac{rL\Delta}{T}}\right).\ \text{Therefore, the complexity to find an }\epsilon\text{-nuclear norm stationary point of }f\text{ is }O(r^2L\sigma^2\Delta\epsilon^{-4})\text{ in the stochastic setting and }O(rL\Delta\epsilon^{-2})\text{ in the deterministic setting}.
key_lemmas.role: Public endpoint: parameter choices for Theorem 4.1.

proof.description: Substitute the printed eta schedule into Theorem 4.1.
Set B=1 and the printed beta schedule to obtain the stochastic displayed rate.
Set sigma to zero and use the deterministic eta schedule from the corollary.
Translate the two rates into the printed stationarity complexities.

key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Theorem 4.7. Under Assumptions 3.2 and 3.3, if we apply Algorithm 1 with }\eta_t=\eta,\text{ then }\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(W_t)\|_*]\le \frac{\mathbb{E}[f(W_0)-f(W_T)]}{T\eta}+\frac{L_*\eta}{2}+\frac{2\sigma\sqrt{r(1-\beta)}}{\sqrt{(1+\beta)B}}+\frac{2\sigma\sqrt r}{(1-\beta)T\sqrt B}+\frac{2\eta\beta L_*}{1-\beta}.

Use the SVD identity for M_t and ||U_tV_t^top||_op=1.
Apply the nuclear-norm triangle inequality to replace ||M_t||_* by ||nabla f(W_t)||_* with one more tracking-error term.
Define C_t and convert Lemma A.4 into a nuclear-norm tracking bound.
Expand C_t in the deterministic lag term for t>0 using C_t=\beta C_{t-1}+(1-\beta)\nabla f(W_t).
Factor out beta from the spectral/nuclear lag display.
Add and subtract the previous true gradient and apply the nuclear-norm triangle inequality.
Use Assumption 3.2 to bound the true-gradient nuclear difference by the operator iterate difference.
Substitute the Algorithm 1 update and use the printed operator-norm bound \|U_{t-1}V_{t-1}^\top\|_{op}\le 1.
proof.ref: B.2 update and operator norm substitution

proof.description: Unroll the recursion to the initial lag and the finite geometric sum.
Use C_0=\nabla f(W_0) and bound the finite geometric sum by \beta/(1-\beta).
Combine the stochastic tracking and deterministic lag bounds by the triangle inequality.
Substitute the combined tracking bound into the one-step descent inequality.
Sum over t=0,...,T-1 and bound the geometric beta sum.

key_lemmas.name: corollary_4_8
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Corollary 4.8. Under the same assumptions as Theorem 4.7, we have the following convergence guarantees for Algorithm 1: Stochastic setting: If }B=1,\eta=\sqrt{\frac{(1-\beta)\Delta}{TL_*}},\text{ and }1-\beta=\min\left\{\frac{\sqrt{L_*\Delta}}{\sigma\sqrt{rT}},1\right\},\text{ then }\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(W_t)\|_*]\le O\left(\sqrt[4]{\frac{rL_*\Delta\sigma^2}{T}}+\sqrt{\frac{L_*\Delta}{T}}+\frac{r\sigma^2}{\sqrt{L_*\Delta T}}\right).\ \text{Deterministic setting }(\sigma=0):\text{ If }\eta=\sqrt{\frac{\Delta}{TL_*}},\beta=O(1),\text{ then }\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|\nabla f(W_t)\|_*\le O\left(\sqrt{\frac{L_*\Delta}{T}}\right).\ \text{Consequently, achieving an }\epsilon\text{-nuclear norm stationary point of }f\text{ requires a complexity of }O(rL_*\sigma^2\Delta\epsilon^{-4})\text{ in stochastic setting and }O(L_*\Delta\epsilon^{-2})\text{ in deterministic setting}.

key_lemmas.name: theorem_4_5
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Theorem 4.5. Under Assumptions 4.3, 3.1, and 4.4, if we apply Algorithm 2 with }\eta_t=\eta,\text{ then }f(W_T)-f^*\le \left(1-\frac{\eta}{D_{op}}\right)^T(f(W_0)-f^*)+\frac{rLD_{op}\eta}{2}.\ \text{Thus, to reach the precision }f(W_T)-f^*\le\epsilon,\text{ we can take }\eta=O\left(\frac{\epsilon}{rLD_{op}}\right),\text{ and the complexity is }O(rLD_{op}^2\epsilon^{-1}\log\frac{\Delta}{\epsilon}).

Under the same assumptions as Theorem 4.5, if we apply Algorithm 2 with adaptive learning rates }\eta_t=\frac{\|\nabla f(W_t)\|_*}{rL},\text{ we have }f(W_t)-f^*\le\frac{2rL(f(W_0)-f^*)D_{op}^2}{2rLD_{op}^2+t(f(W_0)-f^*)}.\ \text{Thus, to reach the precision }f(W_T)-f^*\le\epsilon,\text{ the complexity is }O(rLD_{op}^2\epsilon^{-1}).

key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Theorem 4.16. Under Assumptions 4.3, 4.13 and 4.4, if we apply Algorithm 2 with }\eta_t=\eta,\text{ we have }f(W_T)-f^*\le\left(1-\frac{\eta}{D_{\rm op}}\right)^T\Delta+\frac{\eta^2\tilde J T}{2}+\frac{s\eta^2D_{\rm op}r^{3/2}}{6}.\ \text{where }\tilde J=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\left(1-\frac{\eta}{D_{\rm op}}\right)^{T-1-t}J_t,\ J_t=\overline{\mathrm{vec}}(U_tV_t^\top)^\top H_t\overline{\mathrm{vec}}(U_tV_t^\top),\ H_t=\nabla^2f_v(\overline{\mathrm{vec}}(W_t)),\ \text{and }f_v(\overline{\mathrm{vec}}(W_t))=f(W_t).\ \text{Note that }\tilde J\text{ can be viewed as a weighted average of }J_t\text{ and }\tilde J\le \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}|J_t|.\ \text{If }\tilde J\gtrsim s^{1/2}D_{\rm op}^{-1/2}r^{3/4}\epsilon^{1/2}\text{ and }\eta=\min\left\{\frac{D_{\rm op}}{T}\log\frac{T\Delta}{D_{\rm op}^2\tilde J},D_{\rm op}\right\},\ \text{then }f(W_T)-f^*\le \frac{D_{\rm op}^2\tilde J}{T}+\frac{D_{\rm op}^2\tilde J}{2T}\left[\log\left(\frac{T\Delta}{D_{\rm op}^2\tilde J}\right)\right]^2+\frac{sr^{3/2}D_{\rm op}^3}{6T^2}\left[\log\left(\frac{T\Delta}{D_{\rm op}^2\tilde J}\right)\right]^2\le\widetilde O\left(\frac{D_{\rm op}^2\tilde J}{T}\right).\ \text{Thus, it is possible that Muon can reach the precision }f(W_T)-f^*\le\epsilon\text{ with a complexity of }\widetilde O(\tilde JD_{\rm op}^2\epsilon^{-1}).
